science_question: Does a BLS period/epoch fit solely on NASA Kepler Quarter 6 predict negative photometric dips in independent NASA Quarter 7 original PDCSAP flux, without reoptimizing any period/phase after opening Q7? Does the same check also pass known stellar eclipsing binaries?
design: Exploratory source cohort chosen from previously published Kepler confirmed host lists, BEFORE accessing these Q6/Q7 fluxes. No claims of new planet discovery or independent random-field false-alarm rate.

method_frozen.archive: Official MAST original Q6 and Q7 long-cadence FITS, PDCSAP_FLUX, TIME, SAP_QUALITY; quality==0; same independently applied 301-cadence median normalization each quarter
method_frozen.source_hash: sha256 of each actual downloaded original NASA FITS, output and failure preserved
method_frozen.single_test_score: mean per-event locally normalized depth in test Q7, recorded independent of BLS peak significance; empirical one-sided phase-shift fraction with +1 correction
method_frozen.predictive_evidence_threshold: Q7 phase-shift p<=0.01 AND at least 60% of test quarter event windows have positive local depths; this is only within-quarter phase contrast and not mission false-alarm rate.
method_frozen.missing_file_policy: Keep every planned star including Q6 and/or Q7 unavailable status; never substitute a new target.

statistical_reporting.unit_of_inference: Independent host STAR; stars and events can be correlated. Do not use phase-shift count as number of independent stars.
statistical_reporting.primary_endpoint: Number of preselected ten published planet-host stars with available quarters and Q7 predictive evidence. Count unavailable and no-coherent-event stars separately.
statistical_reporting.binary_control: Two previously inspected known stellar EBs. A positive result here shows predictive period coherence is NOT planet validation. Exclude from independent target denominator.
statistical_reporting.null_caveat: Relative phase shifts preserve the original Q7 stellar time series and do not reproduce the mission pipeline false-alarm probability. A low phase-shift fraction is descriptive evidence only.
statistical_reporting.no_p_hacking: No source replacement, duration, period range, event threshold, or Q7 period optimization after outcomes.
expected_limitations: Known planet hosts may have Q6 strongest BLS peak at a binary contaminant, stellar variability or different known planet; no source role is given to BLS.
Quarter-by-quarter median detrending can distort long transits and periods >20d are outside searched range.
Real Kepler transit timing variations can drift relative to a strictly constant-period forecast.
Single-quarter BLS period errors accumulate across many cycles and may produce false Q7 negatives.
Repeatability alone cannot distinguish a planet from an eclipsing stellar binary.
No new planet search or NASA-grade survey completeness estimate.
